articles.title: Film producer Jeremy Thomas was a cross between a kindly Cambridge don and the movie world’s cool uncle
articles.summary: The man behind The Last Emperor had the confidence of an old-fashioned studio boss along with the soul of a cineaste. To say that movie producer Jeremy Thomas was British cinema royalty did not quite do justice to his meritocratic, democratic instincts.
body: Respectively son and nephew of directors Ralph Thomas and Gerald Thomas (of Doctor in the House and Carry On fame), he was born into the industry and as an independent producer combined the confidence of an old-fashioned studio boss with the soul of a cineaste, backing his own instincts and passions, befriending film-makers and doggedly pursuing projects over years.

Thomas won a best picture Oscar for Bernardo Bertolucci’s epic The Last Emperor in 1988, a movie that gained historic western access to Beijing’s Forbidden City and which in its way perfectly reflected Jeremy’s worldview: pioneering, ambitious, intellectually curious, globalist and internationalist. He produced Jerzy Skolimowski’s The Shout in 1978 and with Skolimowski, co-produced the black comic satire Good Boy as recently as 2025. His friendships and allegiances spanned the decades and he was a vital part of European independent cinema.
points: The man behind The Last Emperor had the confidence of an old-fashioned studio boss along with the soul of a cineaste.
To say that movie producer Jeremy Thomas was British cinema royalty did not quite do justice to his meritocratic, democratic instincts.

articles.title: Everybody Wants to F*ck Me review – Taron Egerton is hounded in sharp-toothed dating nightmare
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: It’s Get Out meets the viral Shitty Media Men list in this hugely entertaining mix of dark comedy and stalker thriller with a brilliant alternating turn from Taron Egerton. Everyone knows an Adam.
body: Everyone knows an Adam. He’s not like those other guys, the ones who won’t take no for an answer and speak lasciviously about women to their mates. He’s doing the work, listening to and uplifting female voices, working at an all-female gallery while being constantly aware of his cis white male privilege. He has a Mubi tote bag, reads Edna O’Brien’s Country Girl in Hackney cafes, has a poster of Cléo from 5 to 7 in his apartment and has even named his dog after his favourite Haim sister. He is … a nice guy.
In first-time writer-director Jonathan Schey’s canny debut Everybody Wants to Fuck Me, Adam is also a fraud.

He’s played by Taron Egerton, someone who has recently been finding his footing as an adult actor, whether as more conventional lead of Netflix’s excellent B-movie thriller Carry-On or as the less expected gonzo villain of Netflix’s mid B-movie thriller Apex. But freed from streaming shackles (he’s also led two Apple dramas, one of which I genuinely don’t think anyone knows exists), he’s able to show just how much more he can do in edgier, stranger territory and how far he’s willing to go without blinking. Turns out, pretty far.

articles.title: Jeremy Thomas, British producer of The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, dies aged 77
articles.summary: An outstanding figure in the UK film industry, Thomas was noted for collaborations with directors including Bernardo Bertolucci and David Cronenberg. Jeremy Thomas, the distinguished British producer of films including Sexy Beast, High-Rise and the multi-Oscar-winning The Last Emperor, has died…
body: A representative for Thomas said he died on Friday “peacefully, at his country home in Oxfordshire, surrounded by his family and loved ones”.

Thomas, who started producing feature films in the early 1970s, was known for forging strong creative relationships with acclaimed auteurs, producing a string of films directed by the likes of Nicolas Roeg, David Cronenberg and Bernardo Bertolucci.

The Last Emperor, directed by Bertolucci, was an early triumph for Thomas, winning nine Oscars including best picture. He went on to become a major figure in the British film-making establishment, including a spell as chair of the British Film Institute and winning a Bafta for outstanding British contribution to cinema.

Born in 1949, Thomas’s father, Ralph, was a prolific film director whose work included the popular Doctor in the House series starring Dirk Bogarde, and his uncle Gerald Thomas directed all 30 of the Carry On films. Thomas started out as an assistant editor, working on the Jimmy Cliff thriller The Harder They Come and Ken Loach’s Family Life, before gaining his first producer credit on Mad Dog Morgan in 1976, with Dennis Hopper as the 19th-century Australian outlaw of the title.
points: An outstanding figure in the UK film industry, Thomas was noted for collaborations with directors including Bernardo Bertolucci and David Cronenberg.
Jeremy Thomas, the distinguished British producer of films including Sexy Beast, High-Rise and the multi-Oscar-winning The Last Emperor, has died…

articles.title: Inside ‘Ah Girl,’ the Singapore Drama Built From a Director’s Own Childhood: ‘We Can’t Fly Without First Learning How to Walk’
articles.summary: Ang Geck Geck Priscilla spent more than a decade making “Ah Girl” before she ever made “Ah Girl.” Three short films and a decade of festival labs later, the Singaporean director’s feature debut is a Centrepiece selection at the Toronto Film Festival for its North American premiere, following wins…
body: Writing from a child’s vantage point meant deliberately withholding adult understanding rather than supplying it. Ang says she kept returning to a single question while drafting the script: what does Ah Girl see, feel and think is happening, rather than what the audience needs to be told. Children, she says, register far more than the adults around them assume. “She is absorbing everything,” Ang says of her protagonist. “I want the adults watching the film to try to understand the child.”

That dynamic sharpens around the film’s central dilemma, in which Ah Girl is asked to choose which parent she wants to live with. “Sometimes they are hoping to hear the answer that will make them feel better about themselves,” she says. “A seven-year-old should never have to carry that emotional responsibility.” She adds that the film returns throughout to the gap between listening to a child and making a child responsible for an adult’s decision: “The adults keep asking her what she wants, but very few of them actually stop to ask what she needs.”

articles.title: ‘Diablo’ Animated Series in the Works at Netflix, Blizzard Entertainment
articles.summary: An animated TV series adaptation of Blizzard Entertainment’s popular “Diablo” video game franchise is in development at Netflix. “Diablo” is set the dark world of Sanctuary, where humanity is caught in the eternal conflict between the High Heavens and the Burning Hells.
body: The “Diablo” TV series development news was announced by Blizzard president Johanna Faries during the opening ceremony of BlizzCon 2026 at the Anaheim Convention Center on Saturday. The two-day fan-festival event, which is the first BlizzCon since Microsoft closed its $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard in 2023, is a celebration of all things Blizzard Entertainment, from “Diablo” to “World of Warcraft” to “Overwatch.”

“BlizzCon in and of itself represents so much for all of us to be able to shine a light on all the great work going on at Blizzard,” Faries told Variety in an interview ahead of the event. “We have put a lot of thought into this moment, and why now, and how do we continue to capture and build on the momentum we’re experiencing as an organization.”
Variety will be on the ground at BlizzCon Sept. 12-13 and readers can follow along with our coverage of the event here.

articles.title: Alan Rickman Brought Kids ‘From the Hospital’ to the ‘Harry Potter’ Set, Says Co-Star Gary Oldman: ‘He Knew How Much It Meant’
articles.summary: While Alan Rickman’s legendary “Harry Potter” character, Severus Snape, may have been notoriously hard on the children at Hogwarts, in real life, the actor couldn’t have been more different from the pupil-hating professor.
body: Oldman noted that Rickman believed it was “the most extraordinary thing, that he was in this world that he got to be in, come in every day, and that he knew how much it meant to these kids. So, he wanted to share it.” He continued to call him “the cheerleader of it”: “He was into it, he was doing it, so he was with it and committed to it,” he said.

In a recent interview with EW, the “Darkest Hour” actor also shared that he believes HBO’s forthcoming TV adaptation of the original subject material will be even “more satisfying,” since more of the wizarding world will be able to be covered.

“We had to cut a lot [for the ‘Harry Potter’ movies], and still we could only get the films down to, like, three hours,” Oldman told the outlet. “I believe [the HBO series is] gonna do it pretty much word-for-word.”
Rickman died on Jan. 14, 2016, following a battle with cancer. The actor starred in films including “Die Hard” and “Truly Madly Deeply,” as well as portraying Snape in all the “Harry Potter” films.

articles.title: Oscar-winning film producer Jeremy Thomas dies aged 77
articles.summary: Best known for The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, the British film-maker was celebrated for working with international directors throughout his decades-long career.
body: Oscar-winning producer Jeremy Thomas, whose films included The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, has died aged 77.
The British filmmaker "passed away peacefully" surrounded by family and loved ones at his home in Oxfordshire on Friday, his publicist said in a statement.

Thomas built an international reputation over a career spanning five decades, working with directors including David Cronenberg, Nagisa Oshima, Julien Temple and Nicolas Roeg and backing independent films alongside mainstream successes.
He best known work, Bernardo Bertolucci's The Last Emperor, won nine Academy Awards, including best picture, and earned Thomas an Oscar as producer in 1988.

articles.title: ‘The Fire Within You’ Review: A Monstrous Mama Unleashes in an Admirable but Draining Italian Comedy-Drama Set on a Miserable Christmas Eve
articles.summary: This Venice competitor from Edoardo De Angelis stars Vanessa Scalera as a caustic matriarch hosting family members whom she subjects to constant and withering criticism.
body: Tempers boil during a Christmas Eve dinner in Milan when the family’s overbearing widowed matriarch Angela (Vanessa Scalera) commandeers the kitchen and starts doling out orders, passive-aggressive self-pity, and endless platters of food seasoned with spite and cigarette ash in caustic Italian comedy-drama The Fire Within You.

However, The Fire Within You will be an acquired taste for some given that the constant bickering and offensive stream of bile out of Angela’s mouth may leave some viewers with family issues feeling triggered and desperate to run for the exit, or upstairs to their bedroom to put noise-cancelling headphones on and cuddle the cat. (That last bit may just be me.) Honestly, this makes the episode “Fishes” in The Bear look like a Noel Coward play.

articles.title: How ‘The Shards’ Rethinks the TV Serial Killer
articles.summary: The cast and producers behind the FX and Ryan Murphy teen thriller discuss how this adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis’ 2023 novel delivers its fictional murderer through a series of killer metaphors.
body: Some stories refuse to stay on the page. The Hollywood Reporter’ s Beyond the Book column explores what happens when books make the leap to screen and beyond — unpacking what stayed, changed, how it was done and why it matters with the creatives who made it.

The 2023 young adult novel turned FX series is, similar to his previous work, told through a self-aware narrator, authorial avatar Bret Easton Ellis ( Igby Rigney ). It’s 1981, and the 17-year-old promising writer is in the throes of his senior year at a private Los Angeles college preparatory school when Robert Mallory ( Homer Gere ), a charming and secretive newcomer, arrives. The closeted teen can’t decide whether he wants to be Robert or be with him, but regardless, the timing of Robert’s emergence feels too coincidental to an increasingly paranoid Bret.
